title: Fermi kernel: Im psi(1/2 + i y) = (pi/2) tanh(pi y)
latent_structure: Occupation-number kernel of fermions is the imaginary part of the digamma function on the half-line 1/2 + i R. Equivalent algebraic Fermi factor: 1/(exp(x)+1) = 1/2 - (1/2)*tanh(x/2) with x = 2*pi*y. Master meromorphic object: tanh (or Im psi), not a CSE of the series definition of psi.

function_domains.polygamma: psi(z) meromorphic; poles of residue -1 at z = 0,-1,-2,... (DLMF 5.2.2)
function_domains.tanh: meromorphic; poles at i*(n+1/2)*pi, n integer (none on real axis)

analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: DLMF 5.4.17 symbol table: y: real variable

analytic_domains.statement: 1/2 + I*y is not a nonpositive integer (so psi is defined)
analytic_domains.label: DERIVED
analytic_domains.source: DLMF 5.2.2: psi(z) defined for z != 0,-1,-2,...; Re(1/2+I*y)=1/2 for real y

branch_conventions: principal imaginary part Im; DLMF writes ℑ psi(1/2 + i y)
source_provenance: NIST DLMF 5.2.2 https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.2.E2 (psi pole set, used only as DERIVED)

derived_conditions.statement: psi(1/2 + i y) has no poles for real y
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: poles of psi are z in {0,-1,-2,...}; Re(1/2+iy)=1/2

why_not_cse_lgg: CSE cannot invent the identification of the Fermi occupation with Im psi or with tanh. The two sides have different special-function heads. LGG does not introduce polygamma/tanh as a master kernel.
proposer_leak_risk: Source names psi, tanh, and imaginary part. Do not leak 'Fermi-Dirac occupation', 'Matsubara', or a target compact formula in proposer-visible context. Catalog should cite the identity residual only.
notes: SymPy-writable with whitelist {im, polygamma, tanh, pi, I}. Fermi translation n_F(x)=1/2-(1/pi)*im(psi(1/2+I*x/(2*pi))) is algebraic from tanh(x/2) and 5.4.17; that translation is commentary, not an extra undeclared domain. y=0 is allowed (both sides 0).
